analysis.title: GS Consumer | Morning Trading Update (US)
key_insights: US equity futures point to a modestly firmer open (SPX +25bps, NDX +15bps, RTY +25bps). UST 10-year yield is down 2.5bps to 4.85% and WTI is off 10bps at $88.65, on light newsflow beyond the global Microsoft 365 outage (MSFT -1.5% pre-market).
Post-earnings moves: CBRS +17%, AMAT +60bps, CSCO -2.75%. NVDA is rebounding +2% pre-market.

Today's docket: US PPI, Eurozone GDP, Fed speakers Collins, Bowman, Daly and Jefferson, and the RVTY investor day. Ahead: Warsh on 11/16, NVDA earnings 11/17, retail prints (HD, LOW, TGT, WMT), Tencent and BABA results, and the Trump-Xi meeting 11/18-11/19.
Consumer discretionary lagged the market for the third straight session yesterday and has given up most of its post-election outperformance.

GS says price action looks like the 1H26 regime, partly driven by momentum/factor shifts. 12-month winners have started to outperform, AI positioning is much cleaner, and consumer has less/wrong-way exposure to momentum. GS notes future momentum rebalances should be supportive of consumer.
NKE investor day is Monday-Tuesday, and consumer earnings pick up next week.
DDS (+0.5%) posted a modest EPS and comp beat: EPS $8.38 vs $8.08 consensus, comps +1.0% vs 0% consensus, led by home/furniture, men's and juniors'/children's. No formal EPS or sales guidance.
FLO (-9%) missed on EPS and EBITDA and cut FY guidance deeply. The Nature's Own relaunch is improving more slowly than anticipated, mainly in loaf. Volume was -7.0%.

OFRM (-8%) had modest 3Q revenue and EBITDA beats, overshadowed by a steep FY guide cut tied to the Tractor Wheels recall. Gross margin fell 600 bps to 36.1% on club trade investment, mix and cooler placement costs. The guide implies a sharp 4Q hit.
Street actions: Baird upgrades DPZ. Stifel downgrades LOW, Piper downgrades YETI, Daiwa downgrades APTV, Evercore downgrades FND and TSCO. StoneX initiates BIRK and DECK at Buy.

market_movers.rationale: Baird upgrades DPZ. No rating or rationale is given in the note.
Stifel downgrades LOW ahead of the retail prints next week.
Piper downgrades YETI. No rationale is given in the note.
Daiwa downgrades APTV. No rationale is given in the note.
Evercore downgrades FND. No rationale is given in the note.
Evercore downgrades TSCO. No rationale is given in the note.
FLO fell 9% after an EPS and EBITDA miss and a deep FY guide cut.
OFRM fell 8% on a steep FY guide cut tied to the Tractor Wheels recall.

sector_views.rationale: Discretionary lagged the market for the third straight session and has given up most of its post-election outperformance. GS expects future momentum rebalances to be supportive.

earnings_insights: DDS reported EPS $8.38 vs $8.08 consensus, revenue $1.48B vs $1.48B consensus, comps +1.0% vs 0% consensus. Retail gross margin was flat at 45.3%. SG&A was 30.3% of sales vs 30.0% last year. Ending inventory rose 4%, slightly ahead of sales growth. No formal guidance.

FLO reported EPS $0.10 vs $0.15 consensus, revenue $1.17B vs $1.18B consensus, volume -7.0%. Adjusted EBITDA was $78.9M vs $97.2M consensus, margin 6.8% vs 8.2% consensus. FY EPS guide was cut to $0.63-0.68 vs $0.78 consensus and $0.75-0.85 prior. FY revenue guide was cut to $5.016-5.063B vs $5.09B consensus and $5.070-5.142B prior. FY adjusted EBITDA guide was cut to $415-430M vs $460.6M consensus and $453-481M prior.

OFRM reported 3Q EPS -$0.09 vs -$0.08 consensus, revenue $89.1M vs $88.4M consensus on volume growth of 32%. Adjusted EBITDA was -$1.0M vs -$2.6M consensus. Gross margin fell 600 bps to 36.1%. FY revenue guide was cut to $290-300M vs $320.3M consensus and $327-335M prior. FY adjusted EBITDA guide was cut to -$4.5M to -$7M vs $2.9M consensus and $3-4.5M prior.
Post-earnings moves in the note: CBRS +17%, AMAT +60bps, CSCO -2.75%. No figures are given for these prints.
Upcoming: NVDA earnings 11/17, retail prints (HD, LOW, TGT, WMT), Tencent and BABA results, NKE investor day Monday-Tuesday, RVTY investor day today.

The Microsoft 365 global outage is weighing on MSFT pre-market.
